sample_unit: expert-graded model responses (32 cases x 7 systems)
models_evaluated: seven unnamed frontier multimodal systems accessed via public interfaces

links.outcome: Whether incorrect model answers expressed uncertainty
links.effect: Failing answers were delivered fluently with no expressed uncertainty, i.e., overconfident output on cases graded as failures.
links.quote: Failing answers were delivered fluently and without any expressed uncertainty.

links.outcome: Consistency of answers across systems, runs, and question formats
links.effect: Answers varied across systems and runs and changed with question format; no numeric consistency figures reported in the abstract.
links.quote: Their answers vary across systems and runs, and change with question format.

links.outcome: Frontier model performance on real patient edge cases versus exam-style benchmarks
links.effect: Performance was poor across all seven systems on 32 real cases (224 graded evaluations). Different vendors missed the same findings and converged on the same wrong plans.
links.quote: Performance was poor across all systems, and the failures were shared: different vendors missed the same findings and converged on the same wrong plans.

screen.reason: The study develops and executes an expert-graded benchmark (ClinEdge) evaluating frontier multimodal foundation models on real patient edge cases involving imaging and clinical vignettes to catalogue clinical failure modes.
